bibl.note: One-based viewer images 190–190; printed page numbers are 44 lower. Archive page labels differ from both. The actual images, rather than another witness or uncorrected OCR, supply the readings.

normalization.p: Source spelling, capitalization, punctuation, written ampersands and visible accents are retained. Long s and typographic ligatures are represented by standard s and constituent letters. Letter spacing in display capitals and quotation glyph shapes may be represented schematically. No modern-edition readings are substituted.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one canonical verse, with stable numbering and a link to its existing image region. Source verse order and headings are retained. Couplet grouping and canonical line numbers are editorial. A displaced word may remain within its verse with its position marked.

Both readers checked actual full-page line starts. The regular visible insets are retained, with an additional two-character approximation at verse 2 for the enlarged initial’s exceptional opening inset. This is source layout evidence, not a rule inferred from verse parity.

correction.p: Uncertain readings remain locally marked with unclear or gap. Observations and uncertainties are documented for a different source reader; ink colour alone does not establish erasure or a separate hand.

revisionDesc.change: First reader inspected and transcribed all 36 verses from the source images; independent source review pending.

Independent second source pass checked every extant verse, source heading, page furniture and full-page line starts; corrected supported readings and documented the source layout in W-3.13-second-pass.md.

Focused independent image reinspection of the enlarged opening initial and following letters corrected source capitalization Cum to CUm; remaining opening letters and second-verse layout rechecked before resealing.

lg.label: Elegia XIII. De Junonis Festo.
lg.l: CUm mihi pomiferis conjux foret orta Faliscis;
Moenia contigimus victa, Camille, tibi.
Casta sacerdotes Junoni festa parabant
Per celebres ludos, indigenamque bovem.
Grande morae pretium, ritus cognoscere: quamvis
Difficilis clivis huc via praebet iter.
Stat vetus, & densâ praenubilus arbore lucus.
Adspice; concedas numen inesse loco.
Accipit ara preces, votivaque tura piorum;
Ara per antiquas facta sine arte manus.
Hinc ubi praesonuit sollemni tibia cantu;
It per velatas annua pompa vias.
Ducuntur niveae, populo plaudente, juvencae,
Quas aluit campis herba Falisca suis:
Et vituli, nondum metuendâ fronte minaces;
Et minor ex humili victima porcus harâ:
Duxque gregis cornu per tempora dura recurvo,
Invisa est dominae sola capella Deae.
Illius indicio silvis inventa sub altis
Dicitur inceptam destituisse fugam.
Nunc quoque per pueros jaculis incessitur index;
Et pretium auctori vulneris ipsa datur.
Quâ ventura Dea est, juvenes timidaeque puellae
Praeverrunt latas veste jacente vias.
Virginei crines auro gemmâque premuntur;
Et tegit auratos palla superba pedes.
More patrum Grajo velatae vestibus albis
Tradita supposito vertice sacra ferunt.
Ore favent populi, tunc cum venit aurea pompa:
Ipsa sacerdotes subsequiturque suas.
Argiva est pompae facies. Agamemnone caeso,
Et scelus & patrias fugit Halesus opes.
Jamque pererratis profugus terrâque, fretoque,
Moenia felici condidit alta manu.
Ille suos docuit Junonia sacra Faliscos.
Sint mihi, sint populo semper amica suo.
